item.title: UWF to celebrate Darrell Gooden Stadium construction milestone Wednesday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The University of West Florida will host a topping out ceremony Wednesday to mark a major construction milestone for the new Darrell Gooden Stadium. The event, scheduled for 10:30 a.m. at PenAir Field on the UWF Pensacola Campus, will celebrate the placement of the final structural beam — a traditional construction milestone marking the completion…
item.content:encoded:
The University of West Florida will host a topping out ceremony Wednesday to mark a major construction milestone for the new Darrell Gooden Stadium. The event, scheduled for 10:30 a.m. at PenAir Field on the UWF Pensacola Campus, will celebrate the placement of the final structural beam — a traditional construction milestone marking the completion of a building's structural framework.

Attendees will have the opportunity to sign the final beam before it is raised into place as part of the ceremony. The stadium project represents a significant investment in UWF's athletic and campus facilities infrastructure.

Media are invited to cover the event. PenAir Field is located at 11000 University Parkway in Pensacola. For more information, contact UWF at news@uwf.edu or 850-503-6510.

item.title: Gulf Shores approves deal to keep Fat Tuesday celebrations going

The approval formalizes an accord between Gulf Shores and the Krewe & Commerce Parade Alliance (KCPA), the organization that coordinates the…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Gulf Shores has green-lit a memorandum agreement to continue hosting Mardi Gras Fat Tuesday festivities through 2027 and beyond, following Monday's city council meeting, according to WKRG News 5.

The approval formalizes an accord between Gulf Shores and the Krewe & Commerce Parade Alliance (KCPA), the organization that coordinates the annual celebration. The move ensures the popular festival will remain part of the city's annual event calendar for years to come.

Fat Tuesday draws crowds to the Alabama Gulf Coast community each year as part of the broader Mardi Gras season celebrations that take place across the Gulf region.

item.title: Georgia man travels to Destin to witness SS United States sinking, reconnecting with mother's 1957 voyage
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Georgia resident made the trip to Destin this week to witness the deliberate sinking of the SS United States, a historic ocean liner—motivated by a deeply personal connection. After discovering memorabilia from his late mother's 1957 voyage aboard the ship, he felt compelled to be present as the vessel met its final fate. The SS United States,…
item.content:encoded:
A Georgia resident made the trip to Destin this week to witness the deliberate sinking of the SS United States, a historic ocean liner—motivated by a deeply personal connection. After discovering memorabilia from his late mother's 1957 voyage aboard the ship, he felt compelled to be present as the vessel met its final fate.

The SS United States, once a crown jewel of American maritime history, has been positioned off the coast of Okaloosa County as part of a planned scuttling operation. The ship's sinking marks the end of an era for a vessel that carried thousands of passengers across the Atlantic during the golden age of ocean travel.

For this man, the discovery of his mother's mementos—preserved artifacts from her own crossing nearly seven decades ago—transformed the ship's demise from a distant news story into a moment of personal significance. His journey to Destin represents a final tribute to both the ship's legacy and his mother's memory.

item.title: SS United States sinking moved to Wednesday due to weather
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Okaloosa County has accelerated plans to sink the SS United States off the coast of Destin, moving the operation to Wednesday from its originally scheduled date, according to a county announcement. The decision comes as unsafe weather conditions threaten to delay the controlled sinking of the former American ocean liner. The SS United States, an…
item.content:encoded:
Okaloosa County has accelerated plans to sink the SS United States off the coast of Destin, moving the operation to Wednesday from its originally scheduled date, according to a county announcement. The decision comes as unsafe weather conditions threaten to delay the controlled sinking of the former American ocean liner.

The SS United States, an iconic mid-20th century passenger ship, has been slated for artificial reef creation off the Florida Panhandle. The vessel will be positioned to serve as an artificial reef structure, a project that has drawn interest from divers and marine enthusiasts in the region.

While Okaloosa County officials cited weather as the primary reason for moving up the timeline, no additional details about specific conditions or the exact Wednesday date were provided in the announcement.

item.title: USPS Reveals 2027 Stamp Designs, Including Pat Summitt, Willie Mays Honors
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Postal Service announced stamp subjects for 2027 on Monday, featuring a mix of sports legends, cultural celebrations, and whimsical designs that will roll out over the coming year. Among the honorees is Pat Summitt, the legendary University of Tennessee women's basketball coach who won eight national championships and 1,098 games during…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Postal Service announced stamp subjects for 2027 on Monday, featuring a mix of sports legends, cultural celebrations, and whimsical designs that will roll out over the coming year.

Among the honorees is Pat Summitt, the legendary University of Tennessee women's basketball coach who won eight national championships and 1,098 games during her 38-year tenure. Summitt, who died in 2016, will be remembered on a stamp featuring an oil portrait created by artist Roberto Parada. The announcement also includes a stamp honoring Willie Mays as part of the Postal Service's Black Heritage series—the 50th in that long-running program. Mays, widely considered baseball's greatest all-around player, passed away in 2024. The stamp design references classic baseball cards and includes imagery of his famous over-the-shoulder catch from the 1954 World Series.

Other 2027 releases will feature Lunar New Year's Year of the Goat, a new Love stamp inspired by folk art with bright geometric shapes, and a 16-stamp pane depicting magical unicorn scenes. The USPS said this is a partial list, with additional stamp subjects to be announced in coming weeks and months. Design details remain preliminary and subject to change, according to the agency's announcement.

item.title: Pensacola to be Featured on 'Wheel of Fortune' This Week
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola is getting national airtime this week as one of five Florida destinations showcased on "Wheel of Fortune" during a special "Live More Floridays"-themed takeover. The show, hosted by Ryan Seacrest and co-hosted by Vanna White, will feature Pensacola alongside Kissimmee, St. Pete-Clearwater, Florida's Treasure Coast, and Tampa across…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola is getting national airtime this week as one of five Florida destinations showcased on "Wheel of Fortune" during a special "Live More Floridays"-themed takeover. The show, hosted by Ryan Seacrest and co-hosted by Vanna White, will feature Pensacola alongside Kissimmee, St. Pete-Clearwater, Florida's Treasure Coast, and Tampa across episodes airing November 9-13.

According to Visit Pensacola, this marks the second consecutive year the destination has been featured on the iconic game show as part of a partnership between VISIT FLORIDA and Sony Pictures Television. The partnership aims to introduce viewers across the country to Florida's diverse offerings beyond theme parks and beaches.

"Pensacola has an incredible story to tell, and partnerships like this give us an opportunity to share it with audiences across the country," said Nicole Stacey, Vice President of Destination Development for Visit Pensacola. "We're thrilled to showcase the experiences that make our corner of Florida unique, from our beautiful beaches and historic downtown to the people who make visitors feel right at home."

Viewers can watch the episodes in syndication, or stream them on Peacock, Hulu, and Hulu on Disney+. Fans who watch can enter a bonus round puzzle at wheeloffortune.com for the chance to win one of five Florida vacations.

item.title: Navy Federal Launches Annual Toys for Tots Drive Through Local Branches
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Navy Federal Credit Union is kicking off its 29-year partnership with Marine Toys for Tots, opening more than 345 branches nationwide as collection sites for new, unwrapped toys through December 7. The Pensacola area has several Navy Federal locations that will participate in the annual holiday drive. The credit union is backing the effort with a…
item.content:encoded:
Navy Federal Credit Union is kicking off its 29-year partnership with Marine Toys for Tots, opening more than 345 branches nationwide as collection sites for new, unwrapped toys through December 7. The Pensacola area has several Navy Federal locations that will participate in the annual holiday drive.

The credit union is backing the effort with a $50,000 donation to Toys for Tots this year, on top of contributions from employees and members. Last year, the partnership resulted in more than 34,000 toys collected for disadvantaged children across the country. According to Navy Federal, there's an increased need this year for toys suitable for infants and preteens, including sports equipment, electronics, and creative sets.

"For 29 years, our team members and members have come together in support of Toys for Tots to help make the holidays brighter for children and families in the communities we serve," said Elizabeth O'Brien, senior vice president of Military Affairs & Strategic Partnerships at Navy Federal. The partnership reflects the credit union's commitment to military families and community support.

Interested donors can drop off new, unwrapped toys at any participating Navy Federal branch through December 7. For a full list of participating locations in the Pensacola area and beyond, members can contact their local branch or visit Navy Federal's website.

item.title: Baptist Health Care Ramping Up Nurse Recruitment for Hospital Expansion
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Baptist Health Care is launching an active recruitment drive for registered nurses across its hospitals, medical parks, and clinics, citing growing patient volumes and the organization's ongoing expansion efforts. The health system plans to add 40 acute care beds to its Baptist Hospital campus, which is driving the hiring push. The recruitment…
item.content:encoded:
Baptist Health Care is launching an active recruitment drive for registered nurses across its hospitals, medical parks, and clinics, citing growing patient volumes and the organization's ongoing expansion efforts. The health system plans to add 40 acute care beds to its Baptist Hospital campus, which is driving the hiring push.

The recruitment effort is open to experienced nurses, new graduates, and those seeking career advancement. "A great nursing career is more than a job," said Joyce Nichols, the organization's vice president and chief nursing officer. "It's about being part of a team where your contributions are valued and your work has meaning."

Baptist Health Care is hosting open interview sessions for new graduate registered nurses on Thursdays—Nov. 19, Dec. 3, 10, and 17—from 10 a.m. to noon at the Bear Family Foundation Health Center, 6th floor, 125 Baptist Way in Pensacola. A broader nursing hiring event is also scheduled for Thursday, Jan. 7, 2027, from 3 to 6 p.m. at the same location. Candidates interested in learning more or applying can visit ebaptisthealthcare.org/jobs.

item.content:encoded:
The City of Milton will close all municipal offices Wednesday, November 11, to observe Veterans Day, with normal business operations resuming Thursday, November 12. Residential sanitation collection schedules will not be affected.

The Santa Rosa County Veterans Memorial Foundation is hosting a Veterans Day Ceremony and wreath-laying at Veterans Memorial Plaza (5191 Willing Street) starting at 11 a.m., with activities expected to wrap up by noon. The ceremony honors the service and sacrifice of the nation's veterans.

Following the ceremony, the community is invited to American Legion Post 78 (6025 Spikes Way in Milton) for a flag retirement ceremony, bonfire, and cookout. Grover's Restaurant is providing food, with service from Santa Rosa County 4-H Club members and volunteers. For more details, contact vetplaza@santarosa.fl.gov.

item.title: Gulf Breeze Will Do Awards $52K+ in Grants to 10 Community Projects
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Gulf Breeze Will Do distributed more than $52,000 in grants to 10 community projects on Sunday, Nov. 8, after an anonymous member stepped forward with an extra contribution to fully fund every finalist. The organization had $46,500 available from membership contributions, but the 10 finalists requested more than $52,000 combined. When a member…
item.content:encoded:
Gulf Breeze Will Do distributed more than $52,000 in grants to 10 community projects on Sunday, Nov. 8, after an anonymous member stepped forward with an extra contribution to fully fund every finalist.

The organization had $46,500 available from membership contributions, but the 10 finalists requested more than $52,000 combined. When a member donated nearly $6,000 to close the gap, Gulf Breeze Will Do was able to award 100 percent of requested funding to all finalists. "This is exactly why Gulf Breeze Will Do exists," Leslie Perino, the organization's president, said in a statement. "To see our members come together to make a difference in our community is incredibly rewarding."

The grants span four categories: art, recreation and sports; education; hardship support services; and public safety. Recipients include Gulf Breeze Middle School Band (for a transport trailer), Gulf Breeze High School biology program (for reusable frog dissection models), Soundside High School's ESE Department (for a student business program), and Gulf Breeze Elementary School (for AED machines and a water fountain replacement). The Santa Rosa Education Foundation also received funding for its Take Stock In Children laptop program.

Gulf Breeze Will Do received 18 grant applications this year requesting over $112,000. Volunteer committees reviewed submissions and selected the 10 finalists, who presented projects at the annual meeting where members voted on funding awards.

item.title: Pensacola Debris Crews Will Work Through Veterans Day
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola’s hurricane debris collection will continue through the Veterans Day holiday as the city works toward completing its first pass through neighborhoods. The city said in a November 9 update that its debris contractor was in the fourth week of the first round of collection. That pass is expected to be…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola’s hurricane debris collection will continue through the Veterans Day holiday as the city works toward completing its first pass through neighborhoods.


The city said in a November 9 update that its debris contractor was in the fourth week of the first round of collection. That pass is expected to be complete in late November, with a second round beginning shortly afterward.


During the second pass, residents can expect to see smaller debris haulers working narrow streets, cul-de-sacs and interior areas off main roads, the city said.


More than 541,850 cubic yards of debris had been collected within city limits, according to the update. The figure had also appeared in an earlier city report.


Regular sanitation collection for City of Pensacola customers will remain on its normal schedule during Veterans Day week, even though City Hall and other administrative offices will be closed Wednesday.


The city anticipates normal bulk and yard waste collections will resume in late December or early January. The Perdido Landfill is not currently accepting vegetative and construction and demolition debris, according to the city.

item.title: Escambia School Foundation Awards More Than $100,000 in Classroom Grants
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Nineteen projects across Escambia County public schools are receiving support through more than $100,000 in classroom grants. The Escambia County Public Schools Foundation awarded $100,012.75 through its Grants for Excellence program for the 2026–27 school year, according to NorthEscambia.com . The projects…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Nineteen projects across Escambia County public schools are receiving support through more than $100,000 in classroom grants.


The Escambia County Public Schools Foundation awarded $100,012.75 through its Grants for Excellence program for the 2026–27 school year, according to NorthEscambia.com.


The projects cover a range of subjects and age groups. At Pensacola High School, one grant supports a hands-on cybersecurity learning and competition space. At Tate High School, another supports robotics.


Other awards include funding for 3D-printing technology at Booker T. Washington High School and an outdoor pollinator habitat and environmental learning laboratory at Ferry Pass Elementary School.


Teachers, schools and departments across the district received the grants. WEAR reported that the program also received support through the Consortium of Florida Education Foundations and a state school district education foundation matching grant program.
